stem:
Sucrose, $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$, reacts with water to form glucose and fructose in reaction A.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest a name for this type of reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain in detail, why glucose and fructose are a pair of structural isomers. Your answer should refer specifically to these two molecules.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Reaction A occurs faster in the presence of an enzyme. This is reaction B.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
The activation energy for reaction B is $+29\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Predict a value for the activation energy of reaction A.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The enthalpy change for reaction A is $-14\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Predict a value for the enthalpy change for reaction B.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Sketch a labelled energy level diagram for reaction B. Use relevant values from (c)(i) and (c)(ii).

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
$1.00\text{ g}$ of sucrose, $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$, is completely combusted. The heat energy produced is used to increase the temperature of $250\text{ g}$ of water inside a calorimeter from $25.0^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $40.7^{\circ}\text{C}$.

These data can be used to calculate the enthalpy change of combustion of sucrose.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term enthalpy change of combustion of sucrose.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the Data Booklet to calculate the enthalpy change, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for the combustion of sucrose.
Assume that all of the heat energy produced is transferred to the water.

Show your working.
